Tomas read it twice, then pinned it above the stove, where he could see it each night before he climbed the stairs.", "w02": "凌晨四点，城市终于安静下来。路灯把空荡的街道照成一条条橙色的河，偶尔有一辆出租车驶过，车灯划开薄雾，又很快消失。便利店的玻璃门后，店员趴在柜台上打盹，冰柜低声嗡嗡作响。远处工地的塔吊亮着一盏红灯，像一颗不肯睡去的星。早点铺的后厨已经透出光来，蒸笼里冒出白气，面粉的味道飘到街口。环卫工人推着车慢慢走过，扫帚擦过地面，沙沙作响。再过一个小时，天会亮，人潮会涌来，而此刻，城市只属于少数醒着的人。", "w03": "- Recursion is when something solves a problem by asking a smaller copy of itself to solve a smaller piece of the same problem.\n- It's like a stack of Russian dolls: you open one doll and find a smaller doll inside, and you keep going until you reach the tiniest doll that can't be opened.\n- That tiniest doll is the \"stop\" rule, and without it the opening would go on forever, so every recursive program needs one."}
